note: Moon & Mars air snapshot: for seven habitat atmospheres, how many NASA PSI table rows were tested nearby, from which investigations, and what is untested. Counts, ranges and record ids only; no table rows. Built by intake/build_moon_mars_air.py.

source.what: the full-data demo's PSI catalog (dashboard_catalog.json) and its habitat rules at that commit

method.near: A PSI table row is near when it records both oxygen and a usable pressure within 3 points of oxygen and 1.5 psi of the preset.
method.oxygenOnly: Rows within 3 points of oxygen whose table gives no usable pressure are counted apart and never placed by pressure.

excluded.reason: Its PSI record has a blank licence field, so this site leaves its rows out of every count.

method.checked: Checked records use the oxygen and pressure printed in their own fields. Records with no pressure are listed by oxygen only. Nearest ranks records with both values by hypot(Δoxygen / 10, Δpsi / 4), the demo's own distance.
method.interpolation: Never. A preset with no tested row nearby says so; no value is estimated between rows.

presets.label: ISS cabin
presets.gravityNote: All 24 PSI combustion investigations are microgravity flight tests or analyses of them.
untested: Whether a cabin material ignites or spreads here: no solid-material flammability test in PSI records both oxygen and pressure near this atmosphere.

How many seconds a flame takes to go out after the fan stops. Saffire I-1, tested close to this atmosphere, went out immediately when airflow stopped; the cited passages give no elapsed time in seconds.

presets.label: Moon base or rover
presets.note: NASA’s challenge: 30% oxygen or more at 10.2 psi or less, to shorten spacesuit pre-breathing.
presets.gravityNote: PSI holds no Moon, 0.16 g combustion data. NASA notes microgravity and normal-gravity results could bound intermediate gravity: use the microgravity rows here as one bound and normal-gravity results (for example Saffire-II’s 1-g columns) as the other. E-FIELD Flames (PSI-22) mimicked partial gravity with an electric field; LUCI and FM2 are future sources not yet in PSI.
